title: Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target Array
summary: Given an integer array target with all elements initially zero, determine the least number of operations needed to transform the initial array into the target array.
statement: Given an integer array target with all elements initially zero, determine the least number of operations needed to transform the initial array into the target array. An operation consists of incrementing each element in a chosen subarray by one.
constraints: Start from an all-zero array of target’s length.
One operation increments every position in a chosen contiguous subarray; return the minimum operations to form target.
hints: Visualize target as horizontal unit-height layers.
An operation must start whenever the current height rises above the previous height.
Add each positive adjacent rise, treating the height before index zero as zero.
Existing active layers extend through flat or lower heights for free; every new layer start is necessary and sufficient.
editorial: Existing active layers extend through flat or lower heights for free; every new layer start is necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: One full increment plus nested increments on the middle three and center makes the target in three operations.
Three layers begin at index zero and one additional layer begins at the final index, totaling four.
